correctness.rationale: A direct tangent-plane parametrization shows that each row lies on one tangent line to the Veronese conic; its dual conic has equation M1^2-4M0M2 in odd characteristic and reduced equation M1=0 in characteristic two. Rank-two openness proves the reduced prime hypersurface equations. The chart A2=1 gives a degree-two purely inseparable extension by z^2=A0. The quadric singular locus follows from differentiation, normality from Serre R1+S2, and the quartic nonnormality from its rank-one singular divisor. Primitive integral H reduces to the square of Q. Exact symbolic and finite-field tests were replayed from the package; finite tests are corroboration.

originality.rationale: Six actual mathematical-record searches and source-to-claim comparisons, along with the accessible deduplication ledger, identify no implication covering the characteristic-two monomial quartic scroll result. The strongest same-family source (Oeding–Raicu) restricts its main statements to characteristic zero; the nearest positive-characteristic quartic-to-quadric analogy (van Geemen–Marrani) concerns different homogeneous varieties. A specialized unlocated tangent-scroll source remains a genuine priority risk, not a proof of novelty.
residual_risks: A specialized pre-2016 account of rational normal scroll tangential varieties in characteristic two may contain an equivalent equation; no complete bibliographic census is claimed.
Previously published char-two quadric degenerations of other homogeneous tangential varieties provide motivation and reduce the scope of any broad novelty claim.
Deduplication history before the accessible current-week ledger was not fully retrievable; best-knowledge comparison used available claims and published records.

value.rationale: The smooth quartic rational normal scroll is a basic minimal-degree projective surface; tangential geometry and its base-change behavior are natural invariants, not arbitrary slices. The theorem exhibits a degree-4 to degree-2 jump, a normality reversal, a purely inseparable tangency map, and a doubled flat special fiber, together giving a precise and geometric boundary to characteristic-zero results on Segre–Veronese tangential varieties. It is not claimed as a general classification or mere computer count.
